subject: ela
intro: This worksheet covers the whole Key Ideas and Details cluster for literature: asking and answering questions with text evidence (3.RL.A.1), finding the central message or lesson (3.RL.A.2), and describing characters and how their actions drive events (3.RL.A.3). Items are grouped by standard and get harder toward the end of each group.

items.prompt:
Read the story.

The fire alarm rang during math, so Mr. Diaz led the class calmly out the side door to the field.

WHY did the class go outside?
items.answer: The class went outside because the fire alarm rang.

steps: The question asks WHY.
The story says "The fire alarm rang."
That is the reason they left.

items.prompt:
Read the story.

Yuki packed her paints, a wide brush, and an easel and headed to the lake.

WHAT is Yuki most likely going to do?
items.answer: Yuki is most likely going to paint a picture at the lake.

steps: The clues are "paints, a wide brush, and an easel."
These are for painting.
So she is going to paint.

items.prompt:
Read the story.

The bakery ran out of bread by nine because a big school order came in early.

WHY did the bakery run out of bread?
items.answer: The bakery ran out because a big school order came in early.

steps: The question asks WHY.
The story says "a big school order came in early."
That order used up the bread.

items.prompt:
Read the story.

When the campfire would not light in the wind, Priya cupped her hands around the match to block the breeze, and the flame caught.

HOW did Priya get the fire to light?
items.answer: Priya cupped her hands around the match to block the wind, and the flame caught.

steps: The question asks HOW.
She "cupped her hands around the match to block the breeze."
Blocking the wind let it light.

items.prompt:
Read the story.

The class could not agree on a pet until Sam suggested a class fish, which no one was allergic to. Everyone cheered.

WHY was the fish a good choice, according to the story?
items.answer: The fish was a good choice because no one was allergic to it.

steps: The question asks WHY the fish worked.
The story says "no one was allergic to it."
That is why everyone agreed.

items.prompt:
Read the fable.

An oak tree bragged it was stronger than the little reeds. A storm blew in; the reeds bent and lived, but the stiff oak cracked and fell.

What is the lesson of this fable?
items.answer: The lesson is that bending and being flexible can help you survive better than being stiff and proud.

steps: The proud oak was "stiff"; the reeds could bend.
The reeds "lived" and the oak "fell."
Flexibility beat stubborn pride.

items.prompt:
Read the story.

Eva wanted to quit after missing three free throws, but she stayed after practice each day. By the playoffs she made nine out of ten.

What central message does this story teach?
items.answer: The message is that practice and not giving up lead to improvement.

steps: Eva almost quit but "stayed after practice each day."
She improved to "nine out of ten."
Persistence and practice paid off.

items.prompt:
Read the folktale.

A rich man mocked a poor farmer for sharing his small meal with a stranger. That stranger, secretly a king, later rewarded the kind farmer and ignored the rich man.

What lesson does this folktale teach, and which detail shows it?
items.answer: The lesson is that kindness and generosity are rewarded. The kind farmer who shared his meal was rewarded by the king, while the mocking rich man was ignored.

steps: The farmer shared even though he was poor.
The stranger, "secretly a king," "rewarded the kind farmer."
Generosity was rewarded; mockery was not.

items.prompt:
Read the story.

Grandpa let his prize tomatoes go so he could spend the summer teaching the neighbor kids to garden. His own garden was smaller that year, but six new gardens sprang up on the block.

State the central message and explain how Grandpa's choice shows it.
items.answer: Message: sharing what you know can grow something bigger than what you give up. Grandpa gave up his prize tomatoes, but his teaching led to "six new gardens" on the block.

steps: Grandpa gave up his own prize tomatoes.
He spent the summer "teaching the neighbor kids to garden."
His giving created "six new gardens."

items.prompt:
Read the story.

When the class hamster escaped, calm Nadia crouched still and waited while others chased it in circles. The hamster crept right to her, and she scooped it up.

Describe Nadia and explain how her action solved the problem.
items.answer: Nadia is calm and patient. Instead of chasing the hamster, she stayed still and waited, so it came to her and she caught it.

steps: Nadia is "calm" and stayed "still."
Others chased it, but she "waited."
Her patience let the hamster come to her.

items.prompt:
Read the story.

Greedy Milo took two turns on the swing every time, so the other kids stopped playing with him and the swings sat empty.

How does Milo's greed change what happens?
items.answer: Milo's greed makes the other kids stop playing with him, so the swings end up empty.

steps: Milo "took two turns" every time.
So the other kids "stopped playing with him."
His greed left the swings empty.

items.prompt:
Read the story.

Determined Ana practiced her flip on the mat every recess for a month, even after falling many times. At the show, she landed it perfectly and the crowd cheered.

Describe Ana and explain how her actions lead to the ending.
items.answer: Ana is determined and hardworking. Because she practiced every recess despite falling, she was able to land her flip perfectly at the show.

steps: Ana "practiced her flip... every recess for a month."
She kept going "even after falling many times."
Her effort led her to "landed it perfectly."

items.prompt:
Read the story.

At first, jealous Ben ignored the new student who was better at soccer. But when the new kid passed Ben the ball for the winning goal, Ben felt ashamed of his jealousy and offered a handshake.

Describe how Ben changes and how his actions show it.
items.answer: Ben changes from jealous to friendly. At first he "ignored" the new student, but after the winning pass he "felt ashamed" and "offered a handshake," showing he let go of his jealousy.

steps: At first Ben is "jealous" and "ignored" the new kid.
After the assist he "felt ashamed of his jealousy."
He "offered a handshake," showing the change.

items.prompt:
Read the story.

Proud Captain Lee refused advice and steered the little sailboat straight into a fog bank. Lost, he finally listened to young Mai, who used the stars to guide them home by midnight.

Describe both characters and explain how their actions shape the events.
items.answer: Captain Lee is proud and stubborn, and his refusal to take advice steers the boat into the fog and gets them lost. Mai is clever and calm, and her action of using the stars guides the boat safely home by midnight.

steps: Lee is "proud" and "refused advice," so they got lost in the fog.
Mai "used the stars to guide them."
Her action fixed the problem Lee's pride caused.

items.prompt:
Read the story.

The power went out during the school play. Instead of panicking, quick-thinking Rosa handed out the flashlights from the prop box and asked the audience to hold up their phones. The show went on, and everyone said the glowing stage looked magical.

Using the story, ask and answer one question about WHY the show could continue, and describe Rosa with one trait that fits her actions.
items.answer: WHY the show continued: because Rosa handed out flashlights and asked the audience to hold up their phones for light. Trait: Rosa is quick-thinking (or resourceful), shown by how she solved the blackout on the spot.

steps: WHY: the show went on because Rosa provided light with "flashlights" and phones.
Trait: she is "quick-thinking" and resourceful.
Her calm actions kept the play going.
